analysis: Documentation-only PR touching two files. In docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md, line 689 changes the gpt-oss-20b sizing row (the K/V float32 on 23 of 24 layers row becomes bf16 K/V on all 24 layers). The values are halved: fixed state 6.03 MB to 3.15 MB, full rows 49,152 B/token to 24,576 B/token, and file at 6,144 tokens 308.0 MB to 154.1 MB. In docs/reference/configuration.md (patch hunk at head line 594), the MLX_QUANTIZED_CONSTANT_CACHE row gains a sentence saying a bf16 GPT-OSS checkpoint keeps bf16 activations, so the constant cast cache does not apply. No code, endpoint, crypto, authorization, TTL, scope-salt or SSD at-rest policy changes. The T-041 SSD prefix-cache posture (HMAC-keyed names, 30-minute TTL, KEK-rooted AES-GCM, coordinator-authored cacheSalt, DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill switch) is not altered by the documented text. The sizing change is an informational layout figure that describes the on-disk checkpoint size per file. I could not verify it against source here, because the underlying Swift code is not in the supplied evidence. The configuration.md patch excerpt is truncated, but the file's changed-range map is complete and shows a single changed line. No security regression or threat-model gap was identified. The remaining integration question is only whether the documented bf16 dtype matches the actual implementation. That is documentation accuracy rather than a security conclusion, so no deeper review is needed.
